cases.case: Provisioning supports serving several formats
cases.what: One Content Hosting Configuration can carry several distribution configurations, each with its own entry point and content type, and all of them are listed as media entry points in Service Access Information.

cases.case: Formats share common media files
cases.what: All distribution configurations of a Content Hosting Configuration serve the same ingested content, so DASH and HLS manifests can reference the same CMAF files.

cases.case: Formats may or may not share media resources
cases.what: The AF places no constraint on whether the entry points of different distribution configurations share media resources.

cases.case: Same CMAF content to different Media Players
cases.what: Several entry points with different content types for the same ingested content are offered to the client in Service Access Information.

noted: Release 17 M1 and M5 APIs. Clause 4.8 is misattributed to clause 4.7.4.8 in the packet (heading extracted as a paragraph).

requirements.name: Procedures for downlink media streaming / General

cases.case: M3d interactions for content hosting configuration
cases.what: The AF sends each Content Hosting Configuration, and the server certificates it references, to its configured AS at M3 when the configuration is created, updated or destroyed.

cases.case: M4d resource identifiers to the Application Provider
cases.what: The AF returns the Content Hosting Configuration with the distribution base URLs it assigned in the create response and on retrieval.

cases.case: M5d resource identifier to the Application Provider
cases.what: The AF returns the provisioning session identifier, under which the Media Session Handler fetches Service Access Information at M5, in the Location header and body of the create response.

cases.case: M2d resource identifier to the Application Provider
cases.what: The AF assigns no M2d ingest address: for push ingest it nominates no ingest base URL, and for pull ingest it only echoes the origin supplied by the Application Provider.

cases.case: No M3d and no M2d/M4d reservations when content is hosted by an AS in the external DN
cases.what: The AF has no mode for content hosted by an AS in the external DN; it always configures its configured AS at M3, so the condition is not met.

cases.case: AF and AS interact to allocate ingest and distribution resources
cases.what: The AF configures its AS at M3 with the Content Hosting Configuration of the provisioning session.

cases.case: AS returns resource identifiers to the AF, which passes them to the Application Provider
cases.what: The AS returns no resource identifiers; the AF derives each distribution base URL from its own configuration (AS canonical hostname and path prefix) and returns that to the Application Provider.

cases.case: Server Certificates configured in the AS at M3d
cases.what: Before sending a Content Hosting Configuration the AF uploads to the AS each server certificate it references, keyed by provisioning session and certificate identifier.

cases.case: Content Preparation Templates configured in the AS at M3d
cases.what: The AF has no Content Preparation Template resources and configures none in the AS.

cases.case: Content Hosting Configuration provided to allocate ingest and distribution resources
cases.what: The AF sends the Content Hosting Configuration to the AS at M3 on create and update.

cases.case: AS returns resource identifiers to the AF, which passes them to the Application Provider
cases.what: The AS returns no resource identifiers; the AF derives each distribution base URL from its own configuration (AS canonical hostname and path prefix) and returns that to the Application Provider.

noted: M3 uses the 5G-MAG pre-standard 3gpp-m3/v1 API; the AF chooses the M4d base URL itself and the AS returns no reservation identifiers.

cases.case: AF limits the updatable parameters
cases.what: On update the AF overwrites canonicalDomainName and baseURL of every distribution configuration with its own values, so the Application Provider cannot change them; all other properties are replaced as supplied.

cases.case: Remove the configuration from every AS that succeeded when another fails
cases.what: Each AS is configured independently; when one fails, the configuration is not removed from those that succeeded.

cases.case: Failure response naming media formats that could not be accommodated
cases.what: The AF answers the create request before the AS has replied at M3 and only logs an M3 failure, so it never reports media formats that could not be accommodated.

requirements.name: Provisioning Session provisioning / Destroy Provisioning Session resource operation

cases.case: Destroy Provisioning Session releases resources, purges cached data and destroys sub-resources
cases.what: Deleting a provisioning session removes its Content Hosting Configuration and certificates from the AS, which purges the session's cache when its configuration is deleted, deregisters its consumption reporting configuration and frees the session in the AF.

noted: Release 17 M1 API under 3gpp-m1/v2: the DELETE is answered 202, not the 204 of TS 26.510 (the status code is judged with the API). The AF sends no purge of its own; the purge is the AS handling of the M3 DELETE. msaf_delete_content_hosting_configuration re-initialises the AS delete queue on every call, which can drop a delete still queued for another session (code-derived, not observed).

requirements.name: Content Hosting Provisioning procedures / Create Content Hosting Configuration

cases.case: Push ingest: ingest baseURL nominated by the AF and returned
cases.what: The AF never reads the pull flag and nominates no ingest base URL for push ingest; whatever the Application Provider sends is kept.

cases.case: DistributionConfiguration.baseURL assigned by the AF and returned
cases.what: The AF overwrites any supplied baseURL with one it builds from scheme, host and path prefix, and returns it on create and retrieve.

cases.case: AF generates a resource identifier for the new configuration
cases.what: The configuration is identified by the content-hosting-configuration URL of its provisioning session, and the provisioning session identifier is used as its identifier on the AS.

cases.case: 201 with the resource URL in the Location header
cases.what: The AF answers a successful create with 201 and the request URL in the Location header.

cases.case: Response body with the current state including AF-set fields
cases.what: The 201 body is the stored configuration including the canonicalDomainName and baseURL the AF assigned.

cases.case: Pull ingest: ingest baseURL returned unchanged
cases.what: A supplied ingest baseURL is checked to be an http or https URL and returned unchanged.

cases.case: domainNameAlias matches a Subject Alternative Name of the referenced certificate
cases.what: The AF does not compare domainNameAlias with the Subject Alternative Names of the referenced certificate and never answers 400 for a mismatch.

cases.case: 400 on create when domainNameAlias does not match the certificate
cases.what: The AF does not compare domainNameAlias with the Subject Alternative Names of the referenced certificate and never answers 400 for a mismatch.

cases.case: Create failure: body not JSON or failing validation answered 400
cases.what: A body that does not parse as JSON or fails validation is rejected with 400 and a ProblemDetails body.

cases.case: Create failure: unknown provisioning session answered 404
cases.what: A POST under a provisioning session that does not exist is rejected with 404, naming the session identifier in invalidParams.

cases.case: Create failure: referenced certificate not found mapped to the most similar status code
cases.what: A configuration that references a certificate the AF cannot find is answered 404, a code TS 29.500 clause 5.2.7.2 gives to a target resource that does not exist, although the target exists and the error is in the request body (400 for client errors).

cases.case: Create failure: ProblemDetails body
cases.what: Every error response carries a ProblemDetails body with type, title, status, detail and instance.

cases.case: Create failure: Content-Type application/problem+json
cases.what: Error responses with a ProblemDetails body are sent with Content-Type application/problem+json.

cases.case: Create failure: cause attribute
cases.what: No error response carries the cause attribute, including for the common errors of TS 29.500 Table 5.2.7.2-1 such as an invalid message format (400) or a system failure (500).

cases.case: Create failure: invalidParams for schema errors and a malformed ingest base URL
cases.what: Schema validation failures and a malformed ingest base URL name the offending parameter in invalidParams.

cases.case: Create failure: invalidParams for a malformed entry point
cases.what: A malformed entry point relative path or an empty profiles array is rejected with 400 but without invalidParams.

noted: The 201 is sent before the AS has confirmed the configuration; a POST on a session that already has a configuration replaces it and also answers 201.
The AF does not require an ingest baseURL when pull is true.

cases.case: Destroy releases resources, purges cached content and deletes configurations
cases.what: DELETE frees the configuration in the AF and sends an M3 DELETE for it to the AS, which removes it there.

noted: Each call re-initialises the AS delete queue, so a deletion still queued for another session would be dropped.

requirements.name: Content Hosting Provisioning procedures / Purge Content Hosting cache

cases.case: Purge with POST and a regular expression in the body
cases.what: POST on content-hosting-configuration/purge is accepted with an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body (415 otherwise) and the body is relayed to the AS.

cases.case: Cached content matching the regular expression purged
cases.what: The AF relays the purge to every AS serving the provisioning session, which removes the matching cache entries.

cases.case: Purge failure: unknown provisioning session answered 404
cases.what: A purge for a provisioning session that does not exist is answered 404, naming the session identifier in invalidParams.

cases.case: Purge failure: body not form-urlencoded answered 415
cases.what: A purge request whose Content-Type is not application/x-www-form-urlencoded is answered 415.

cases.case: Purge failure: no usable Application Server answered 500
cases.what: When the Application Server state cannot be obtained, the AF answers 500.

cases.case: Purge failure: error from the Application Server relayed
cases.what: An error status returned by the Application Server (400, 404, 413, 414, 415, 422, 500 or 503) is relayed with its invalidParams.

cases.case: Purge on an Application Server hosting another provisioning session
cases.what: For every other provisioning session hosted by the same Application Server, the AF sends 500 ("not assigned to an Application Server") on the purge request while still forwarding the purge, so a purge that succeeds can be answered with 500.

cases.case: Purge failure: ProblemDetails body
cases.what: Every error response carries a ProblemDetails body with type, title, status, detail and instance.

cases.case: Purge failure: Content-Type application/problem+json
cases.what: Error responses with a ProblemDetails body are sent with Content-Type application/problem+json.

cases.case: Purge failure: cause attribute
cases.what: No error response carries the cause attribute, including for the common errors of TS 29.500 Table 5.2.7.2-1 such as an invalid message format (400) or a system failure (500).

cases.case: Purge failure: malformed regular expression answered 400 (clause 7.6.4.3)
cases.what: A regular expression that does not compile is rejected with 400 by the Application Server and the AF relays that response.

cases.case: Purge failure: empty or pattern-less body answered 400 (clause 7.6.4.3)
cases.what: The AF does not inspect the body: an empty body or one without a pattern is forwarded and purges the whole cache instead of being rejected with 400.

noted: Basis: TS 26.512 V17.10.0 clause 6.3 delegates to TS 29.501 V17.9.0 clause 4.8, whose clause 4.8.1 delegates the status codes to TS 29.500 V17.16.0 clause 5.2.7.
422 is not in TS 29.500 V17.16.0 Table 5.2.7.1-1; the Application Server never returns it (-162).
TS 29.500 V17.16.0 clause 5.2.7.2 requires the cause attribute for the errors listed in Table 5.2.7.2-1; TS 29.501 V17.9.0 clause 4.8.2 says it should be included.

cases.what: A GET for the protocols of a provisioning session that does not exist is answered 404; the protocols document itself cannot fail.

cases.what: Every error response carries a ProblemDetails body with type, title, status, detail and instance.

cases.what: Error responses with a ProblemDetails body are sent with Content-Type application/problem+json.

cases.case: Read Content Protocols failure: cause attribute
cases.what: No error response carries the cause attribute, including for the common errors of TS 29.500 Table 5.2.7.2-1 such as an invalid message format (400) or a system failure (500).

noted: Basis: TS 26.512 V17.10.0 clause 6.3 delegates to TS 29.501 V17.9.0 clause 4.8, whose clause 4.8.1 delegates the status codes to TS 29.500 V17.16.0 clause 5.2.7.
TS 29.500 V17.16.0 clause 5.2.7.2 requires the cause attribute for the errors listed in Table 5.2.7.2-1; TS 29.501 V17.9.0 clause 4.8.2 says it should be included.

requirements.name: Operations / Content caching

cases.case: Caching rules in the Content Hosting Configuration
cases.what: The AS ignores cachingConfigurations; every M4d response is cached with the same fixed proxy settings.

cases.case: Caching rules (cachingConfigurations: urlPatternFilter, first match, noCache, maxAge, statusCodeFilters)
cases.what: cachingConfigurations is accepted in the configuration but never turned into cache rules; every resource is cached the same way.

cases.case: domainNameAlias: serve under the alias
cases.what: Creates a virtual server for the alias host name with the same locations as the canonical one.

cases.case: First matching CachingConfiguration applies
cases.what: The AS never evaluates CachingConfiguration urlPatternFilter, so no first-match rule is applied.

cases.case: No CachingConfiguration matches: apply origin caching directives
cases.what: With no caching configuration applied, the AS proxy cache follows the Cache-Control and Expires directives received from the origin, falling back to fixed validity times only when the origin sends none.

cases.case: Defaults when no rule matches and the origin gives no directives
cases.what: Uses fixed defaults for all resources (200 responses kept for one day, any other status for one minute); the clause requires defaults based on the media resource type.

cases.case: Caching directive: noCache or cache for maxAge
cases.what: The AS does not apply noCache or maxAge from any caching directive.

cases.case: maxAge relative to ingest time t_ingest
cases.what: No maxAge is applied by the AS, so no lifetime is computed from the ingest time.

cases.case: t_ingest from the M2d Date header
cases.what: The AS does not derive an ingest time from the M2d Date header for any provisioned maxAge.

cases.case: Stale after t_ingest + maxAge, not served from cache
cases.what: With no provisioned maxAge applied, the AS has no t_ingest + maxAge staleness rule.

cases.case: Compensate for origin clock skew
cases.what: The AS does nothing to compensate for clock skew between origin and itself, for example no max-stale directive is added.

cases.case: Signal maxAge via Expires or Cache-Control at M4d
cases.what: The AS adds no Expires or Cache-Control header derived from a provisioned maxAge; it passes through whatever the origin sent.

cases.case: Translate noCache into no-cache/no-store or max-age=0
cases.what: The AS never reads noCache, so no such directive is generated.

cases.case: Origin HTTP header fields not forwarded by default
cases.what: The proxy configuration hides none of the origin's response header fields, so they are passed on at M4d; clause 7.6.4.2 says that by default origin header fields are not forwarded (the originCacheHeaders flag it names to change this is not defined in table 7.6.3.1-1).

cases.case: No origin directives: default caching directives by media resource type
cases.what: Without origin directives the AS caches every successful response for one day and any other status for one minute, whatever the media resource type.

cases.case: Caching rules per distribution configuration for transport resources
cases.what: The AS ignores caching configurations in distribution configurations.

cases.case: Use CachingConfigurations[].urlPatternFilter for transport resources
cases.what: The AS never evaluates urlPatternFilter.

cases.case: First matching caching configuration applies (transport resources)
cases.what: The AS never evaluates caching configurations, so no first-match rule is applied.

requirements.name: Content Hosting Provisioning procedures / Create Content Hosting Configuration

cases.case: Create Content Hosting Configuration
cases.what: The tools create a Content Hosting Configuration from a JSON file (m1-client), from the new-stream flow or from the management UI.

cases.case: Create uses HTTP POST with a ContentHostingConfiguration body
cases.what: The request is a POST to .../content-hosting-configuration with the configuration serialised as JSON.

cases.case: Push ingest: IngestConfiguration.baseURL not set by the Application Provider
cases.what: The configuration layer always sends an ingest baseURL, because a media entry requires a non-empty ingest URL even when pull is false; it then reads back the AF-assigned value. The m1-client command sends the configuration file as given.

cases.case: DistributionConfiguration.baseURL omitted from the creation request
cases.what: The new-stream flow and the management UI build distribution configurations without a baseURL, and the m1-session update path strips baseURL and canonicalDomainName before sending.

cases.case: Create response may include the ContentHostingConfiguration
cases.what: The client accepts a 201 with an empty body or with the configuration, and parses the configuration when present.

cases.case: Pull ingest: IngestConfiguration.baseURL nominated by the Application Provider
cases.what: With pull set to true the tools always send the ingest baseURL; the configuration layer refuses an empty one.

cases.case: domainNameAlias matches a Subject Alternative Name of the referenced certificate
cases.what: The configuration tools add each distribution's domainNameAlias to the certificate it references and have that certificate issued from a signing request carrying the alias as a Subject Alternative Name, so the alias matches the certificate.

noted: The configuration layer serialises any baseURL or canonicalDomainName it holds for a distribution, including values read back from the AF, so a configuration it re-sends can carry them.

m1-session new-stream with SSL raises a TypeError before creating anything: session.py line 844 calls createNewCertificate with extra_domaqin_names, a keyword the method does not accept. m1-client sends the operator's configuration file unchecked.

requirements.name: Content Hosting Provisioning procedures / Update Content Hosting Configuration properties

cases.case: Update request with HTTP PUT or PATCH
cases.what: The client sends a full replacement with PUT or a JSON Patch (application/json-patch+json) with PATCH.

cases.case: Update response 200 (OK) with the resource
cases.what: For PUT the client treats only 204 as success, following the OpenAPI annex; a 200 with the updated resource, as the clause text gives, is reported as a failed update. PATCH accepts 200.
cases.conflict: TS 26.512 V17.10.0 clause 4.3.3.4: "If the procedure is successful, the 5GMSd AF shall respond with a 200 (OK) and provide the content of the resource in the response, confirming the successful update operation." / TS 26.512 V17.10.0 clause C.3.5, updateContentHostingConfiguration (PUT): responses '204' 'Updated Content Hosting Configuration' and '404'. / TS 26.512 V17.10.0 clause C.1: "This Annex shall take precedence when being discrepant to other parts of the present document with respect to the encoding of information elements and methods within the API(s)." This does not clearly reach response status codes.

cases.case: Writeable properties except domainNameAlias may be updated
cases.what: The tools can update any property of the configuration; the m1-session update path removes the read-only canonicalDomainName and baseURL first.

cases.case: Update (PATCH)
cases.what: Sends PATCH with application/json-patch+json and expects 200 with the template.

noted: Nothing stops a changed domainNameAlias from being sent in an update.

cases.conflict: TS 26.512 V17.10.0 clause 4.3.3.5: "If the procedure is successful, the 5GMSd AF shall respond with a 200 (OK) response message." / TS 26.512 V17.10.0 clause C.3.5, destroyContentHostingConfiguration (DELETE): responses '204' 'Destroyed Content Hosting Configuration' and '404'. / TS 26.512 V17.10.0 clause C.1: "This Annex shall take precedence when being discrepant to other parts of the present document with respect to the encoding of information elements and methods within the API(s)." cases.case: domainNameAlias of every distribution set to a Subject Alternative Name of an uploaded referenced certificate
cases.what: The tools upload a certificate only when a distribution carries an alias, and that certificate is issued with the alias as a Subject Alternative Name, so the alias of each distribution that references it matches.

cases.case: Configuration layer: certificate change reflected in the Content Hosting Configuration
cases.what: The configuration layer creates a new Server Certificate resource for a changed certificate, but compares distributions' certificate references by presence only, so the Content Hosting Configuration is not re-sent to reference the new certificate.

cases.case: Operations of Table 7.3.2-1
cases.what: All five operations of the table are invoked: POST create, POST ?csr reserve, GET retrieve, PUT upload and DELETE destroy.

cases.case: Create Server Certificate (POST certificates)
cases.what: Sends an empty body, expects 200 and takes the certificate identifier from the Location header.
cases.locator: clause 7.3.2, Table 7.3.2-1, row Create Server Certificate

cases.case: Reserve Server Certificate request
cases.what: Reserve sends POST to certificates?csr=true with a JSON array of domain name aliases, or an empty body when there are none.

cases.case: Reserve Server Certificate response
cases.what: The certificate identifier is taken from the Location header and the response body is kept as the CSR PEM.

cases.case: Retrieve Server Certificate (204 when reserved)
cases.what: Retrieve sends GET to certificates/{certificateId}, returns the PEM on 200 and reports a reserved, not yet uploaded certificate on 204.

cases.case: Upload Server Certificate (PUT PEM)
cases.what: Upload sends PUT with the PEM certificate as application/x-pem-file; the certificate is produced from the AF's CSR by a local CA or ACME signer that keeps the CSR's public key.

cases.case: Destroy Server Certificate (DELETE)
cases.what: Destroy sends DELETE to certificates/{certificateId} and accepts 204 or 202.

noted: Success is recognised only on 200, which matches the OpenAPI in TS 26.512 V17.10.0 clause C.3.2.
The local CA signer gives every issued certificate serial number 1 ; no clause governs this.

requirements.name: Content Hosting Provisioning API / Resource structure

cases.case: Content Hosting Provisioning base path
cases.what: Content hosting requests go to {apiRoot}/3gpp-m1/v2/provisioning-sessions/{provisioningSessionId}/content-hosting-configuration.

cases.case: Sub-resource path appended to base path
cases.what: The provisioning session identifier is substituted and the content-hosting-configuration (or /purge) sub-resource appended for each operation.

cases.case: Operations of Table 7.6.2-1
cases.what: All operations of the table are invoked with the listed methods: POST, GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE and POST purge.

cases.case: Create Content Hosting Configuration (POST)
cases.what: Create sends POST with the JSON Content Hosting Configuration and treats 201 as success, keeping any returned body.

cases.case: Retrieve Content Hosting Configuration (GET)
cases.what: Retrieve sends GET and parses the returned Content Hosting Configuration on 200; 404 returns nothing.

cases.case: Update Content Hosting Configuration (PUT)
cases.what: Update sends PUT with a full replacement Content Hosting Configuration and treats 204 as success.

cases.case: Update Content Hosting Configuration (PATCH)
cases.what: Patch sends PATCH with an application/json-patch+json document and parses the returned configuration on 200.

cases.case: Purge Content Hosting Configuration cache (POST)
cases.what: Purge sends POST to content-hosting-configuration/purge as application/x-www-form-urlencoded, but writes the regular expression into the body without percent-encoding it, so expressions containing &, +, % or = are altered, and sends an empty body when no expression is given.

cases.case: Destroy Content Hosting Configuration (DELETE)
cases.what: Destroy sends DELETE and accepts 204 or 202; 404 is reported as nothing to delete.

noted: The purge request body is judged under the purge statement.
The 200 count and 204 none-purged responses are handled.

requirements.name: Data model / ContentHostingConfiguration resource

cases.case: ContentHostingConfiguration data model
cases.what: The tool models name, ingestConfiguration and distributionConfigurations, but differs from the table in three places: cachingDirectives is an optional array instead of one mandatory object, supplementaryDistributionNetworks is a list of tuples with value DISTRIBUTION_NETWORK_EMBMS instead of objects with NETWORK_EMBMS, and edgeResourcesConfigurationId is missing.

cases.case: Table 7.6.3.1-1 properties
cases.what: The tool models name, ingestConfiguration and distributionConfigurations, but differs from the table in three places: cachingDirectives is an optional array instead of one mandatory object, supplementaryDistributionNetworks is a list of tuples with value DISTRIBUTION_NETWORK_EMBMS instead of objects with NETWORK_EMBMS, and edgeResourcesConfigurationId is missing.

cases.case: name 1..1
cases.what: name is a mandatory string in the type and is always set by the tool's builders (generated when not given).

cases.case: ingestConfiguration 1..1
cases.what: ingestConfiguration is mandatory in the type and always sent with pull, protocol and baseURL.

cases.case: pull 1..1
cases.what: pull is a mandatory boolean of ingestConfiguration; the builders set it from the operator's choice, defaulting to true.

cases.case: protocol 1..1
cases.what: protocol is a mandatory URI; the configuration model rejects values outside urn:3gpp:5gms:content-protocol and defaults to http-pull-ingest.

cases.case: ingestConfiguration.baseURL for pull ingest
cases.what: For pull ingest the tool always supplies ingestConfiguration.baseURL.

cases.case: ingestConfiguration.baseURL for push ingest populated by the AF
cases.what: The configuration model requires a non-empty ingest URL even for push ingest and sends it to the AF; it reads back the URL the AF assigns only afterwards.

cases.case: distributionConfigurations 1..1

requirements.name: Network Assistance API / Overview

cases.what: The AF serves the Network Assistance API under /3gpp-m5/v2/network-assistance/ and creates a session resource before any boost can be requested.

requirements.name: Network Assistance API / Resource structure

cases.case: {apiRoot}/3gpp-maf-session-handling/v1/provisioning-sessions/{provisioningSessionId}/network-assistance-sessions/
cases.what: The AF has no Release 19 Network Assistance resource; it serves only /3gpp-m5/v2/network-assistance/.

cases.case: Sub-resource paths {naSessionId} and {naSessionId}/boost-request under the base path
cases.what: The AF routes {naSessionId} (GET, PUT, DELETE) and {naSessionId}/boost-request (POST) under /3gpp-m5/v2/network-assistance/.

cases.case: Sub-resource path {naSessionId}/recommendation
cases.what: The recommendation sub-path is not distinguished: the GET handler ignores it and returns the session.

cases.case: Create with POST
cases.what: POST to the network-assistance collection creates the Network Assistance Session once the PCF accepts it and answers with the session in the body.

cases.case: URL of the created session in the Location header
cases.what: The AF answers a successful create with 200 and no Location header; the table requires the URL in the Location header (the V17.10.0 OpenAPI defines 201 with a required Location).

cases.case: Fetch with GET
cases.what: GET returns 200 with the session, or 404.

cases.case: Update with PUT
cases.what: PUT replaces the session parameters, updates the PCF application session and returns 200 with the session.

cases.case: Update with PATCH
cases.what: PATCH is answered 403 Forbidden.

cases.case: Bit rate recommendation with GET {naSessionId}/recommendation
cases.what: The request is handled as a plain retrieve and returns the NetworkAssistanceSession, not an M5QoSSpecification with a recommendation.

cases.case: Delivery boost with POST {naSessionId}/boost-request
cases.what: The AF asks the PCF to raise the minimum downlink bit rate to the configured boost rate and answers 200 with an OperationSuccessResponse whose success flag says whether the boost is applied; the boost is reverted when the configured period ends.

cases.case: Terminate with DELETE
cases.what: DELETE answers 204, removes the session and deletes its PCF application session; later calls get 404.

requirements.name: Usage of 5GC interfaces and APIs / Usage of N5/N33 for AF-based Network Assistance

cases.case: M5 invocations converted into Policy Authorization invocations
cases.what: Create, update, boost and destroy at M5 become create, update and delete of a PCF application session at N5.

cases.case: PCF responses converted to M5 responses
cases.what: The outcome of the PCF create or boost update decides the M5 answer: the created session, or an OperationSuccessResponse with success true or false.

cases.case: PCF notifications converted to M5 equivalents
cases.what: PCF notifications are only written to the log; nothing is passed to the Media Session Handler.

cases.case: Delivery boost offered
cases.what: The AF offers delivery boosts on a Network Assistance Session and applies them through the PCF.

cases.case: Bit rate recommendation (throughput estimation) offered
cases.what: The AF offers no bit rate recommendation: the recommendation request is handled as a plain retrieve, so no M5QoSSpecification recommendation is returned.

cases.case: Based on existing Policy Templates matching the session
cases.what: Boosts ignore Policy Templates: the boost rate and period come from AF configuration and the session policyTemplateId is never read.

cases.case: Interaction with the PCF by one of the listed methods
cases.what: The AF calls the PCF directly at N5 with Npcf_PolicyAuthorization, after finding the PCF through the BSF.

cases.case: Direct Npcf_PolicyAuthorization at N5
cases.what: The AF invokes Npcf_PolicyAuthorization directly at N5, finding the PCF for the UE address from its cache or the BSF.

cases.case: AF application session context created in the responsible PCF
cases.what: On create the AF looks up the PCF responsible for the UE address of each listed flow and creates an application session context there.

cases.case: Npcf_PolicyAuthorization_Create when no context exists
cases.what: The AF creates a new application session context with Npcf_PolicyAuthorization_Create for each flow of each new session.

cases.case: Derived from the service data flow descriptions and requested QoS
cases.what: The media component carries the flow descriptions and the requested maximum, minimum and desired bit rates.

cases.case: Derived from the referenced Policy Template
cases.what: The policyTemplateId is passed to the media component builder but never used.

cases.case: Exactly one media component per context
cases.what: Each application session context the AF creates carries exactly one media component.

cases.case: One sub-component per M4 application flow
cases.what: Each flow is sent in its own application session context with a single sub-component, instead of as separate sub-components of one media component.

cases.case: Subscribed to Service Data Flow QoS notification control
cases.what: The AF subscribes each PCF application session to the QOS_NOTIF, QOS_MONITORING, SUCCESSFUL_QOS_UPDATE and FAILED_QOS_UPDATE events only, which includes QoS notification control; notifications are only logged.

cases.case: Subscribed to Service Data Flow deactivation
cases.what: The AF subscribes each PCF application session to the QOS_NOTIF, QOS_MONITORING, SUCCESSFUL_QOS_UPDATE and FAILED_QOS_UPDATE events only; it does not subscribe to FAILED_RESOURCES_ALLOCATION, the event that reports service data flow deactivation.

cases.case: Subscribed to resources allocation outcome
cases.what: The AF subscribes each PCF application session to the QOS_NOTIF, QOS_MONITORING, SUCCESSFUL_QOS_UPDATE and FAILED_QOS_UPDATE events only; SUCCESSFUL_RESOURCES_ALLOCATION and FAILED_RESOURCES_ALLOCATION are not requested.

cases.case: Policy Templates determine the QoS references in altSerReqs
cases.what: The AF sends no altSerReqs and no QoS references; Policy Templates play no part in Network Assistance.

cases.case: Priority order of the altSerReqs QoS references
cases.what: The AF sends no altSerReqs, so no priorities are assigned.

cases.case: AF application session context destroyed with the session
cases.what: Destroying the session sends a delete of its PCF application session context.

noted: The AF never reuses an existing context for the same flow; the NEF route is not implemented.
A session with several flows gets one context per flow, so one media streaming session can have several contexts.
TS 29.514 V17.16.0 clause 4.2.3.7: subscription to service data flow deactivation is an events entry set to "FAILED_RESOURCES_ALLOCATION"; the AF does not include that event.

requirements.name: Dynamic Policy provisioning / Policy Template life-cycle

cases.case: Policy Template moved to SUSPENDED
cases.what: The state machine allows READY to SUSPENDED, but nothing in the AF or its management API triggers it.

cases.case: PENDING upon creation
cases.what: A new Policy Template is put into the PENDING state on creation.

cases.case: Validation triggered once mandatory properties are provided
cases.what: The AF moves every new or updated Policy Template from PENDING straight to READY with no validation by the operator.

cases.case: INVALID when the operator does not validate it
cases.what: No validation exists, so no Policy Template is ever moved to INVALID.

cases.case: READY after successful validation
cases.what: The AF moves every new or updated Policy Template from PENDING straight to READY with no validation by the operator.

cases.case: SUSPENDED by the operator; update returns it to PENDING
cases.what: Nothing triggers SUSPENDED; the state machine would accept SUSPENDED to PENDING on update, but the state is never reached.

cases.case: Destroyed in any state
cases.what: Delete moves the template to the null state from PENDING, READY, INVALID or SUSPENDED and then removes it.

cases.case: Status verified before a Dynamic Policy Instance instantiates it
cases.what: At instantiation the AF checks only that the Policy Template exists in the Provisioning Session, not its state, so a template in any state can be instantiated.

cases.case: State in machine-readable form
cases.what: The Policy Template carries its state as an enumerated value.

cases.case: Human-readable reason for the state
cases.what: stateReason has a title and detail only for INVALID and SUSPENDED; for PENDING and READY it is an empty problem detail.

requirements.name: Policy control interactions for Dynamic Policies / Subscription to PCF notifications

cases.case: Subscribed to Service Data Flow QoS notification control
cases.what: The AF subscribes each PCF application session to the QOS_NOTIF, QOS_MONITORING, SUCCESSFUL_QOS_UPDATE and FAILED_QOS_UPDATE events only, which includes QoS notification control; notifications are only logged.

cases.case: Subscribed to Service Data Flow deactivation
cases.what: The AF subscribes each PCF application session to the QOS_NOTIF, QOS_MONITORING, SUCCESSFUL_QOS_UPDATE and FAILED_QOS_UPDATE events only; it does not subscribe to FAILED_RESOURCES_ALLOCATION, the event that reports service data flow deactivation.

cases.case: Subscribed to resources allocation outcome
cases.what: The AF subscribes each PCF application session to the QOS_NOTIF, QOS_MONITORING, SUCCESSFUL_QOS_UPDATE and FAILED_QOS_UPDATE events only; SUCCESSFUL_RESOURCES_ALLOCATION and FAILED_RESOURCES_ALLOCATION are not requested.

cases.case: Subscribed to Service Data Flow L4S enablement
cases.what: The AF subscribes each PCF application session to the QOS_NOTIF, QOS_MONITORING, SUCCESSFUL_QOS_UPDATE and FAILED_QOS_UPDATE events only; it requests no L4S notification.

cases.case: Subscribed to Service Data Flow QoS monitoring enablement
cases.what: The AF subscribes to no QoS monitoring enablement notification; its QOS_MONITORING subscription carries no monitoring parameters.

cases.case: Subscribed to Service Data Flow QoS monitoring results
cases.what: The AF subscribes to the QOS_MONITORING event with event detection as the notification method, but sends neither the QoS monitoring parameters to be measured nor the reporting thresholds that such a subscription carries, so no monitoring is requested; notifications are only logged.

cases.case: For each of the Dynamic Policy Instances it is managing with QoS monitoring ...
cases.what: The AF has no UPF event exposure client.

cases.case: - Service Data Flow QoS monitoring results.
cases.what: The AF has no UPF event exposure client.

noted: TS 29.514 V17.16.0 clause 4.2.3.7: subscription to service data flow deactivation is an events entry set to "FAILED_RESOURCES_ALLOCATION"; the AF does not include that event.

TS 29.514 V17.16.0 (the release the AF's PCF client is built on) has no separate enablement notification: table 5.6.3.7-1 defines QOS_MONITORING as "Indicates PCF to enable Qos Monitoring for the Service Data Flow." The enablement notification of the Release 19 text was not checked in a Release 19 issue of TS 29.514.

requirements.name: Dynamic Policy Provisioning procedures / General

cases.case: New Policy Template not usable before operator verification
cases.what: The AF moves every new Policy Template from PENDING straight to READY with no operator verification, and instantiation does not check the state.

cases.case: PENDING upon creation
cases.what: A new Policy Template is put into the PENDING state on creation.

cases.case: Validation triggered once mandatory properties are provided
cases.what: The AF moves every new or updated Policy Template from PENDING straight to READY with no validation by the operator.

cases.case: INVALID when the operator does not validate it
cases.what: No validation exists, so no Policy Template is ever moved to INVALID.

cases.case: Operator validation (PENDING to READY or INVALID)
cases.what: The AF moves every Policy Template from PENDING straight to READY with no validation; the clause requires the 5GMS System operator to validate it, moving it to READY or INVALID.

cases.case: Update returns the template to PENDING
cases.what: Any update puts the Policy Template back into PENDING (from where it is moved straight to READY, not to operator revalidation).

cases.case: Suspension by the operator (SUSPENDED)
cases.what: The state machine allows READY to SUSPENDED, but nothing in the AF or its management API can trigger it.

cases.case: Destroyed in any state
cases.what: Delete moves the template to the null state from PENDING, READY, INVALID or SUSPENDED and then removes it.

cases.case: Create: only a READY Policy Template may be instantiated
cases.what: The AF checks that the Policy Template exists but not its state; the clause allows only a READY template to be instantiated.

cases.case: Only a READY Policy Template instantiated
cases.what: At instantiation the AF checks only that the Policy Template exists in the Provisioning Session, not its state, so a template in any state can be instantiated.

cases.case: state and stateReason exposed
cases.what: The resource carries state and a stateReason problem detail set on each transition.

cases.case: Update (PUT): success response code
cases.what: Returns 204 No Content with no body.

cases.case: Create: policy triggered in the 5G System (flowDescription)
cases.what: For a flowDescription the AF finds the PCF (from its cache or the BSF) and creates a PCF application session with the flow and the capped bit rates.

cases.case: flowDescription filled in for packet filter flows
cases.what: For a flow given as a packet filter the AF builds permit in/out flow descriptions from the addresses, ports and protocol.

cases.what: Replaces the policy, updates the PCF application session with the new bit rates and returns 200 OK with the resource.

cases.case: Destroy (DELETE /dynamic-policies/{dynamicPolicyId})
cases.what: Removes the PCF application session and returns 204 No Content once the PCF confirms, or 404 Not Found.

requirements.name: Data model / DynamicPolicy resource

cases.case: dynamicPolicyId
cases.what: The AF assigns a new UUID as dynamicPolicyId on creation and keeps it on update.

cases.case: policyTemplateId
cases.what: policyTemplateId is required and must name a Policy Template of the Provisioning Session, whose limits are then applied.

cases.case: serviceDataFlowDescriptions given as flow descriptions
cases.what: serviceDataFlowDescriptions is required and non-empty; each flowDescription (with direction and the UE address) becomes a PCF application session.

cases.case: serviceDataFlowDescriptions given as domain names
cases.what: A service data flow given as a domainName makes the create fail with 400.

cases.case: mediaType
cases.what: mediaType is passed to the PCF media component, VIDEO when absent.

cases.case: provisioningSessionId
cases.what: provisioningSessionId is required and is used to find the Policy Template; an unknown session makes the create fail with 400.

cases.case: qosSpecification
cases.what: The requested bit rates are capped at the Policy Template limits and sent to the PCF; minimum and desired bit rates are passed through.

cases.case: enforcementMethod set by the AF
cases.what: The AF never sets enforcementMethod.

cases.case: enforcementBitrate
cases.what: The AF sets enforcementBitrate to the lower of the Policy Template downlink limit and the requested downlink maximum.

noted: The check meant to reject a policyTemplateId that is not a string is inverted and never fires .

requirements.name: Usage of 5GC interfaces and APIs / Usage of N5/N33 for dynamic policies

cases.case: Dynamic Policies invocations converted into Policy Authorization invocations
cases.what: Create, replace and delete at M5 become create, update and delete of a PCF application session at N5.

cases.case: PCF responses converted to M5 responses
cases.what: The PCF outcome decides the M5 answer: 201 with the instance on success, 401 when the PCF refuses or cannot be reached, 204 once a deletion is confirmed.

cases.case: Interaction with the PCF by one of the listed methods
cases.what: The AF calls the PCF directly at N5 with Npcf_PolicyAuthorization, after finding the PCF through the BSF.

cases.case: Direct Npcf_PolicyAuthorization at N5
cases.what: The AF invokes Npcf_PolicyAuthorization directly at N5, finding the PCF for the UE address from its cache or the BSF.

cases.case: AF application session context created in the responsible PCF
cases.what: On create the AF looks up the PCF responsible for the UE address of each listed flow and creates an application session context there.

cases.case: Derived from the service data flow descriptions and requested QoS
cases.what: The media component carries the flow descriptions and the requested bit rates, capped at the Policy Template limits.

cases.case: Subscribed to Service Data Flow QoS notification control
cases.what: The AF subscribes each PCF application session to the QOS_NOTIF, QOS_MONITORING, SUCCESSFUL_QOS_UPDATE and FAILED_QOS_UPDATE events only, which includes QoS notification control; notifications are only logged.

cases.case: Subscribed to Service Data Flow deactivation
cases.what: The AF subscribes each PCF application session to the QOS_NOTIF, QOS_MONITORING, SUCCESSFUL_QOS_UPDATE and FAILED_QOS_UPDATE events only; it does not subscribe to FAILED_RESOURCES_ALLOCATION, the event that reports service data flow deactivation.

cases.case: Subscribed to resources allocation outcome
cases.what: The AF subscribes each PCF application session to the QOS_NOTIF, QOS_MONITORING, SUCCESSFUL_QOS_UPDATE and FAILED_QOS_UPDATE events only; SUCCESSFUL_RESOURCES_ALLOCATION and FAILED_RESOURCES_ALLOCATION are not requested.

cases.case: Policy Template determines the QoS references in altSerReqs
cases.what: The AF sends no altSerReqs and no QoS references to the PCF.

cases.case: AF application session context destroyed with the dynamic policy
cases.what: Destroying a Dynamic Policy Instance sends a delete of its PCF application session context.

noted: TS 29.514 V17.16.0 clause 4.2.3.7: subscription to service data flow deactivation is an events entry set to "FAILED_RESOURCES_ALLOCATION"; the AF does not include that event.

requirements.name: Consumption reporting / Procedures

cases.case: Check configuration before session start
cases.what: The Service Access Information is fetched before playback is triggered, and reporting is initialised from its consumption reporting configuration when the session starts.

cases.case: Periodic re-check of Service Access Information
cases.what: The Service Access Information is fetched again according to its cache headers and changes are signalled to the reporting controller.

cases.case: Configuration removed
cases.what: After removal the Media Session Handler no longer submits reports (it drops them), although its timer keeps firing.

cases.case: Configuration added during a session
cases.what: A configuration that appears after the session started is ignored (previous configuration null returns early), so reporting is not activated until the next session.

cases.case: Decision at session start
cases.what: A decision is drawn from samplePercentage at session start, but it only gates the periodic report timer: in a session drawn out of reporting, the report the Media Stream Handler produces at the end of playback is still submitted to the AF.

cases.case: Decision when the configuration changes
cases.what: On a change the reporting is stopped for 0 percent, started for 100 percent and redrawn only when going from 0 to above 0; other changes (for example 100 to 50) trigger no new decision.

cases.case: 100 percent activates
cases.what: A samplePercentage of 100 or more always activates consumption reporting.

cases.case: Random draw below 100 percent
cases.what: A random number uniformly distributed in 0 to 100 is drawn and reporting is activated when it is lower than samplePercentage.

cases.case: Report at start
cases.what: See the start-of-consumption case: a report is requested when playback becomes ready.

cases.case: Report at end
cases.what: A report is produced when playback ends.

cases.case: Periodic report
cases.what: A report is requested every reportingInterval.

cases.case: Report on location change
cases.what: A report is triggered on a cell-information update, but cell information is requested only once when the adapter initialises, so later location changes are not detected.

cases.case: Report on access network change
cases.what: No handler reacts to a change of access network; accessReporting only controls whether endpoint addresses are included.

cases.case: Interval timer reset on report
cases.what: When a consumption report is received the timer is cancelled and restarted with the current reportingInterval.

cases.case: Timer disabled at session end
cases.what: The consumption reporting timer is stopped when playback ends and when the client session is reset.

cases.case: Time-ordered list
cases.what: Consumption reporting units are appended in the order the media changes, so the list is ordered by start time.

cases.case: Unit start time and duration
cases.what: Each unit carries the selected media (mediaConsumed), a start time and a duration.

cases.case: Contiguous timeline
cases.what: A unit is closed by the first unit in the list with the same media type, even if that unit is already closed; after two switches between reports one earlier unit is never closed and the timeline overlaps.

cases.case: Selected media when not consuming
cases.what: The current unit stays in the list while playback is paused and its duration is extended to the report time, so the selected media is still reported.

cases.case: Unit in exactly one report
cases.what: Closed units are removed after each report and the ongoing unit is repeated as the specification expects, but a unit left open by the closing defect is repeated in every later report.

cases.case: New unit when the media consumed changes
cases.what: Closes the open unit of the same media type and opens a new one on each downstream format change.

noted: Units are also tracked per container MIME type (audio and video separately).

requirements.name: Metrics reporting / Procedures

cases.case: Check configurations before session start
cases.what: The Service Access Information is fetched before playback; reporting is initialised for each client metrics reporting configuration at the start of the session.

cases.case: Periodic re-check of Service Access Information
cases.what: The Service Access Information is fetched again per its cache headers and changes are signalled to the reporting controller.

cases.case: Configuration removed
cases.what: A configuration that disappears from the list has its timer cancelled and its entry removed.

cases.case: Configuration added during a session
cases.what: A configuration that is new in a later Service Access Information has no session entry and no reporter in the Media Stream Handler, so it is not activated until the next session.

cases.case: Decision at session start
cases.what: A decision is drawn per configuration from samplePercentage at session start, but it only gates the periodic report timer: for a configuration drawn out (samplePercentage above 0), the report the Media Stream Handler produces for every configuration at the end of playback is still submitted to the AF.

cases.case: Decision when a configuration changes
cases.what: On a change reporting is stopped for 0 percent and started for 100 percent; other changes (for example 100 to 50) trigger no new random draw.

cases.case: 100 percent activates
cases.what: A samplePercentage of 100 or more activates reporting for that configuration.

cases.case: Random draw below 100 percent
cases.what: A uniformly distributed random number in 0 to 100 is drawn and reporting is activated when it is lower than samplePercentage.

cases.case: Periodic report
cases.what: A report is requested every reportingInterval.

cases.case: Report at end of session
cases.what: A report is produced for every active configuration when playback ends.

cases.case: Reporting window (reportingStartOffset, reportingDuration)
cases.what: The client has no start offset or duration for reporting; periodic reports start after the first interval and continue until the session ends.

cases.case: Interval timer reset on report
cases.what: When a report is received the timer of that configuration is cancelled and restarted with its reportingInterval.

cases.case: Timers disabled at session end
cases.what: All metrics reporting timers are stopped when playback ends.

requirements.name: 5G unicast downlink Media Streaming architecture / Service Access Information for downlink media streaming

cases.case: Entry points announced with the service list (M8d)
cases.what: The application passes a service list entry that may carry entry points, and the client uses them when present and falls back to the entry points of the fetched Service Access Information otherwise.

cases.case: Full Service Access Information announced with M8d
cases.what: The service list entry carries only a provisioning session id and optional entry points; reporting, policy and other configuration are always fetched from the 5GMS AF.

cases.case: Consumption reporting sample percentage
cases.what: The client reports consumption only for the configured percentage of sessions, drawn at random when playback becomes ready.

cases.case: Sample percentage not specified
cases.what: The client data model reads an absent consumption samplePercentage as 0, so no consumption reports are sent instead of all clients reporting.

cases.case: Recommended SDF methods
cases.what: The client does not read the list of recommended service data flow description methods and does not use dynamic policies.

cases.case: Scheme of the 3GPP
cases.what: The client recognises the 3GPP DASH metrics scheme and has a reporter for it.

cases.case: Scheme of a non-3GPP entity
cases.what: Only the 3GPP DASH metrics scheme has a reporter; configurations naming any other scheme are ignored.

cases.case: Scheme not specified
cases.what: An absent scheme is not mapped to the default 3GPP scheme: no reporter is found for it and no metrics are reported.

cases.case: Scheme identified by URI
cases.what: The client identifies a metrics scheme by its URI string, urn:3GPP:ns:PSS:DASH:QM10 for the 3GPP DASH scheme.

cases.case: DNN not specified
cases.what: Metrics reports are sent over the device default network; the client does not select a data network.

cases.case: Consumption reporting interval not specified
cases.what: With no reportingInterval the client does not send the single final consumption report: the report handler starts the periodic timer first and fails on the missing interval.

cases.case: Metrics reporting interval not specified
cases.what: With no reportingInterval the client starts no periodic reporting and does not send the single final metrics report: the report handler restarts the timer first and fails on the missing interval.

cases.case: Metrics sample percentage not specified
cases.what: With no samplePercentage the client starts periodic metrics requests but then drops every metrics report: the report handler dereferences the missing percentage.

cases.case: URL filter not specified
cases.what: The client applies no URL filter, so metrics are reported for all URLs.

cases.case: Metrics of the 3GPP scheme for DASH
cases.what: The client reports the eight DASH quality metrics of the 3GPP scheme (representation switch list, average throughput, initial playout delay, buffer level, playlist, MPD information, playout delay for media start-up, device information) and no others.

cases.case: Quality reporting scheme URN
cases.what: The 3GPP DASH quality reporting scheme URN is used as the scheme identifier.

cases.case: Quality report XML format
cases.what: Reports are serialised as the 3GPP reception report XML and posted over HTTP to the configured metrics server.

cases.case: Quality report MIME type
cases.what: Reports are posted with Content-Type application/xml, not application/3gpdash-qoe-report+xml.

cases.case: Network assistance server address
cases.what: The client has no network assistance support and does not read a network assistance server address.

cases.case: Slice scope not specified
cases.what: The client applies no slice scope, so metrics are collected and reported regardless of the network slice.

cases.case: Content type of an entry point
cases.what: The content type of each entry point is read and used to pick the DASH entry point.

cases.case: Profile indicators of an entry point
cases.what: Profiles are parsed into the data model but not used to select among entry points.

cases.case: Precedence of an entry point
cases.what: There is no precedence property; the first DASH entry point is used.

cases.case: Communication service type not specified
cases.what: The client applies no communication service type filter, so metrics are collected and reported for any service type.

noted: The announcement format (m8.json) is application-defined; the client receives the provisioning session id and optionally entry points.

cases.case: Polling for updated Service Access Information guided by Expires and Cache-Control max-age
cases.what: The Media Session Handler re-requests the Service Access Information after the shorter of the max-age (less any Age) and Expires periods, sending If-None-Match and If-Modified-Since.

noted: When neither header is present a default interval of 10 seconds from the handler configuration is used. The period from Expires is taken as an absolute difference, so an Expires value in the past still schedules a later poll. Including these headers in every response falls on the AF.

requirements.name: Media delivery session life-cycle / Explicit media session handling initiation/termination

cases.case: Explicit initiation method at M6 or M11
cases.what: There is no explicit session handling initiation method; a start-playback message carrying a service list entry plays that role.

cases.case: External service identifier as input
cases.what: The start message carries a provisioning session id, not an external service identifier.

cases.case: Globally unique identifier allocated
cases.what: The Media Session Handler allocates a random UUID as the media delivery session identifier on each start.

cases.case: Identifier used with the AF
cases.what: The identifier is passed to the Media Stream Handler and carried as the recording session id of every QoE metrics report sent to the 5GMS AF.

cases.case: Identifier used with the AS
cases.what: Media requests at M4 carry a separate random CMCD session id, not the media delivery session identifier.

cases.case: MSH initialises the Media Access Function
cases.what: The Media Session Handler does not create the Media Stream Handler instance; the application initialises it beforehand and the Media Session Handler then sends it the entry points.

cases.case: Media delivery initiated by passing the entry point
cases.what: The Media Session Handler passes the entry points to the Media Stream Handler, which attaches and plays them.

cases.case: Session id on M6 interactions
cases.what: No M6 interface exists; the messages between the application-side adapter and the Media Session Handler do not carry a session identifier and clients are told apart by caller uid.

cases.case: Session id on M7 interactions
cases.what: The application calls the player adapter without a session identifier.

cases.case: Session id on M11 interactions
cases.what: After the one start message, Messenger messages between the Media Session Handler and the Media Stream Handler do not carry the session identifier.

cases.case: Explicit termination method
cases.what: There is no terminate method; unbinding the Messenger service clears the Media Session Handler state.

noted: Earlier form: START_PLAYBACK_BY_SERVICE_LIST_ENTRY_MESSAGE.
Earlier form: the service list entry holds provisioningSessionId.

TS 26.512 V19.3.0 clause 11.4.3.2: "In both cases, the QoEReport@recordingSessionId attribute shall be populated with the media delivery session identifier." Consumption reports and Service Access Information requests do not carry it.
The identifier is used afterwards only as recordingSessionId in QoE reports.
Earlier form: unbinding resets all client state.

requirements.name: HTTP protocol version / 5GMS AF

cases.case: HTTP/1.1 endpoints at M1 and M5

cases.case: HTTP/2 endpoints at M1 and M5
cases.what: M1 and M5 are served over HTTP/2.

cases.case: HTTP/2 starting mechanisms of RFC 7540 section 3
cases.what: Differs from the specification; details for members.

cases.case: TLS supported at M1 and M5
cases.what: The SBI server offers TLS, with ALPN, when the server certificate and key are configured.

cases.case: HTTPS used in preference to cleartext
cases.what: Differs from the specification; details for members.

cases.case: ETag and Last-Modified on resource responses
cases.what: GET and create responses that return a resource (Provisioning Session, Content Hosting Configuration, protocols, certificates, policy templates, metrics and consumption configurations, Service Access Information, Dynamic Policy, network assistance session reads) set ETag and Last-Modified.

cases.case: ETag and Last-Modified on every response with a body
cases.what: Some responses with a body carry neither header: the network assistance session create response, delivery boost results, problem documents and the management listing.

cases.case: If-None-Match and If-Modified-Since on all endpoints
cases.what: Only the Service Access Information GET honours If-None-Match and If-Modified-Since (answering 304); other endpoints ignore them.

noted: RFC 7540 section 3 gives three ways to start HTTP/2: the HTTP/1.1 Upgrade with the "h2c" token for "http" URIs (3.2), TLS-ALPN for "https" URIs (3.3) and prior knowledge (3.4); the first is missing.
The ETag value is an unquoted hex digest.

cases.case: {FQDN} is the AF FQDN exposed to the requesting client
